description:
After the reference-impl extraction epic lands (each server crate gets a public, feature-gated `memory::MemoryBackend`), writing examples becomes nearly trivial. This bead's scope was originally to invent examples from scratch; the new scope is to wrap the public reference impls with thin example narratives.

## Updated scope (post-extraction-epic)

Suggested minimum (unchanged from original):

- `jmap-base-client/examples/session_fetch.rs` — `new_plain` → `fetch_session` → print capabilities. Uses wiremock under the hood OR a real test endpoint with `JMAP_TEST_URL` env var. No backend needed.

- `jmap-mail-client/examples/mailbox_list.rs` — spin up `jmap_mail_server::memory::MemoryBackend` in-process behind an `axum`/`hyper` test server, point a `JmapClient` at it, query mailboxes, print. ~50-80 LOC.

- `jmap-chat-client/examples/sse_listen.rs` and `examples/ws_loop.rs` — same shape, using `jmap_chat_server::memory::MemoryBackend`. ~80-120 LOC each.

- `jmap-mime/examples/parse_eml.rs` — parse a hand-supplied .eml file, print the resulting `jmap_mail_types::Email`. ~40 LOC. No backend needed; pure parser demo.

- `jmap-server/examples/dispatcher_minimal.rs` — register one method with a stub handler, dispatch a synthetic request, print response. Uses a no-op handler. ~60 LOC. NOT a full backend; demonstrates the dispatcher's job specifically.

## Why this bead is reduced (not cancelled)

The examples themselves still need to be written and reviewed for narrative clarity. They are NOT the same code as the reference impls — they're thin wrappers that demonstrate the client-side and dispatcher-side flow against the reference impls.

Each example becomes a doc-test target in lib.rs (`#[doc = include_str!("../examples/foo.rs")]`) or is referenced by `//! See `examples/foo.rs` ...`.

## Acceptance

- 6 example files land (one per crate as listed).
- Each example compiles, runs, produces sane output.
- Each example is ≤ 120 LOC and reads as a narrative, not a tutorial.
- `cargo build --workspace --examples` clean.
- `cargo run --example session_fetch -p jmap-base-client` (etc.) succeeds.
- README.md for each affected crate has a one-line link to its `examples/` directory.

## Depends on

The reference-impl extraction epic landing first (so that the public `memory::MemoryBackend` types exist to be referenced by the client examples).

## Why this is now low-risk

Without the extraction epic, examples for client/server crates required either (a) inventing demo backends inline (cookie-cut sprawl), (b) using wiremock and JSON fixtures (test-shaped, not example-shaped), or (c) requiring a deployed real server (unworkable for example code). With the extraction, examples just import the public reference impl. Clean.

LABELS: examples, publish-readiness, review
notes:
[2026-05-11 /do-beads] Decomposed into 5 child beads (.17.1 through .17.5), one per crate per the bead Suggested minimum enumeration. .17 stays open as meta-tracker and depends on all five children.
Workflow-workaround human label dropped (2026-05-11, Mark, batch-clean of stale labels). Both children .17.4 and .17.5 are now resolved via option A; the parent's filtering concern (do-beads re-surfacing it as ready) becomes moot once the children close and the parent auto-resolves.
Body-framing correction (2026-05-11, Mark): the description's 'Suggested minimum' list for .17.4 (mailbox_list.rs) and .17.5 (sse_listen.rs + ws_loop.rs) says 'spin up MemoryBackend behind an axum/hyper test server'. That framing was aspirational and pre-dated noticing that the workspace's *-server crates are deliberately transport-less.

The actual decisions recorded on the children are kit-aligned:

  - .17.4 → option (A): wiremock + hand-written Mailbox/get JSON fixture. No axum/hyper involved.
  - .17.5 → option (A) adapted: hand-rolled tokio TcpListener for SSE, hand-rolled tokio-tungstenite accept loop for WS. No axum/hyper involved.

The workspace identity is 'library kit, not server' (see workspace AGENTS.md 'What this workspace builds' section, landed 2026-05-11). HTTP transport lives only in jmap-testjig (epic JMAP-cf7p), which is publish=false. Future /do-beads passes reading the body of this bead should treat the 'axum/hyper test server' language as superseded by these children's recorded option-A decisions.
